question: Does reducing added-noise SNR increase or decrease estimated delay magnitude, conditional on waveform, true lag and noise structure?
scope: one participant, three existing verified NWB sessions; no population inference
templates: 36: three sessions x first/middle/last artifact-free correct trial x first channel of four bundles; 1-2s of each trial with real padding
noise_only_control: 200 independent pairs per noise type, no common template and no true delay; report magnitude distribution only
primary_outcome: mean over windows of absolute estimated delay, not absolute value of the mean signed delay
contrasts: paired magnitude change versus 20 dB for each fixed template/noise realization
paired changes between adjacent SNR levels
effect_labels: increase >1 ms, decrease <-1 ms, otherwise within +/-1 ms; descriptive threshold fixed before results, not a significance test
uncertainty: template mean IQR describes fixed-template heterogeneity; conditional Monte Carlo SE uses independent noise replicates within templates, not overlapping windows
validation: baseline recovery and direct-original verification across templates, signs, noise types, noise modes and SNR; preserve source hash
limits: added-noise SNR is not physiological SNR; no independent biological sample claims; fixed search bounds may influence low-SNR behavior; no change to E or original estimator
